title: Potato, baked, peel eaten, with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the skin on is a simple, nutritious side dish prepared in the oven until the exterior is golden and crisp. The skin retains most of the fiber and nutrients, while butter adds richness and a source of healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The potato skin contains more fiber, vitamin C, and potassium than the flesh.
Baking preserves more antioxidants than boiling.
Butter enhances flavor but should be used in moderation.
Potatoes are among the most widely consumed root vegetables worldwide.
Baked potatoes are often served as “potato boats” filled with toppings.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The skin provides a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which helps maintain electrolyte balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Skin‑contained vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbohydrates
items.content: Complex starches supply a steady release of energy.

items.title: Beneficial fats from butter
items.content: Butter adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that aid absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter increases the dish’s calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Individuals with milk sensitivities may experience reactions.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged high‑temperature baking can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen. Avoid over‑browning.

items.title: Sodium considerations
items.content: If salt is added, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, split the potato lengthwise, and add a pat of butter. The skin can be eaten whole or lightly seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw potatoes in a cool, dark place. Store cooked baked potatoes in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat with a little extra butter to retain moisture.
